$comment: The council. Every entry was verified by running it on 2026-07-28 — command, flags,
and a live round-trip. Latencies are for a one-word answer and are a FLOOR, not an
estimate: a real question is minutes, and Codex has been measured exceeding 10 minutes on
a plan review. The council is background work. Nothing waits on it in the foreground.
Every member runs READ-ONLY. codex --sandbox read-only, agy --mode plan, grok with no
tools, claude --print. They advise; they never touch the repo. That is a security
decision, not a convenience: five agents with write access to a tree holding a live
OAuth token is the lethal trifecta with extra seats.
They also run from a neutral scratch directory rather than the repo, so a member cannot
read the project unless the prompt hands it the context deliberately.
No external AI API is used. Every one of these is a CLI on a subscription this machine
already has — which is what AGENTS.md §1 requires.

members.label: GPT-5.6 sol (Codex CLI)
members.note: The other vendor already load-bearing in §10. Reasoning effort pinned per skills/pick-the-model. --skip-git-repo-check is required because the scratch dir is deliberately not a repo — it relaxes a git check, NOT the sandbox, which stays read-only.

members.label: Grok 4.5
members.note: Only grok-4.5 is offered on this account. Web search off so the council reasons rather than retrieves.

members.label: Gemini 3.1 Pro (Antigravity)
members.note: Reached via Antigravity (agy 1.1.7), NOT the gemini CLI — that one now refuses this account outright: 'no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals'. gemini-3.1-pro-high is the highest 3.1 tier offered; there is no -max.

members.label: Fable 5
members.note: A second Claude voice, deliberately not the chairman's.

members.label: Sonnet 5
members.note: Included as a COUNCIL member only. skills/pick-the-model rule 0 pins the top tier for work; a council is the one place a different vantage point is the product, and no council member's answer is adopted without the chairman's synthesis.

chairman.label: Opus 5 (this session)
chairman.note: The chairman is whoever invoked the council — it reads the transcript and writes the synthesis in-session, so nothing is lost to a subprocess boundary. Pinned to opus by settings.json.
